record.paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Is the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on trees well posed? More precisely, for a tree graph equipped with the relevant vertex coupling conditions, can one prove existence, uniqueness, and appropriate continuous dependence for solutions in the natural energy spaces, analogous to the well-posedness theory available for the star-graph case?

evidence.quote: in [24] a generalization of this systems to trees (including star graphs) is studied as a model of cardiovascular system, and in particular it is shown that BBM on a tree is well posed. It is interesting that (see [25]) travelling waves for BBM equation on a tree have been recently constructed for particular vertex conditions. By the way a result of well posedness of NLS on trees in not yet proven, although well plausible; a step in this direction with proof of relevant dispersive estimates is given in [26, 27].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a metric tree graph: a finite or locally finite connected graph with no cycles, in which each edge $e$ is identified with an interval $[0,\ell_e]$ (with $\ell_e\in(0,\infty]$ for unbounded edges), so that $\mathcal{T}$ is a one-dimensional metric space. A function $u:\mathcal{T}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ is identified with a collection $\{u_e\}_{e}$ of functions on the edges. Equip $\mathcal{T}$ with Kirchhoff (free) vertex coupling: at every vertex $v$, the function values along incident edges agree, and the sum of the outgoing derivatives vanishes,
$$\sum_{e\succ v} \partial_e u_e(v,t) = 0.$$
Let $H^1(\mathcal{T})$ denote the energy space of continuous functions on $\mathcal{T}$ whose restriction to each edge belongs to $H^1$, with the natural Hilbertian norm. Consider the Cauchy problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t u(x,t) = -\Delta_{\mathcal{T}}\, u(x,t) + \kappa\, |u(x,t)|^{p-1} u(x,t),\qquad x\in\mathcal{T},\ t\in\mathbb{R}, $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{T}}$ is the edgewise Laplacian with the Kirchhoff vertex conditions above, $\kappa\in\{-1,+1\}$ is the focusing/defocusing sign, and $p>1$ is energy-subcritical, with initial datum $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in H^1(\mathcal{T})$.

Prove (or disprove) that this Cauchy problem is well posed in the energy space $H^1(\mathcal{T})$: namely, that for every $u_0\in H^1(\mathcal{T})$ there exists a unique solution $u\in C([0,T);H^1(\mathcal{T}))$ on a maximal time interval depending only on $\|u_0\|_{H^1(\mathcal{T})}$, that the solution depends continuously on the initial datum, and that the mass $\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{T})}^2$ and the energy
$$E(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_e \int_0^{\ell_e} |\partial_x u_e|^2\,dx + \tfrac{\kappa}{p+1}\sum_e \int_0^{\ell_e} |u_e|^{p+1}\,dx$$
are conserved along the flow, in analogy with the corresponding well-posedness theory available on a star graph.
artifact.status_search_result: Local and global well-posedness of the energy-subcritical NLS in the energy space $H^1$ on general (noncompact) metric graphs—including trees—with Kirchhoff vertex conditions has by now been established as a standard fact, following the Cazenave-style argument combined with the Sobolev embedding $H^1(\mathcal{G})\hookrightarrow L^\infty(\mathcal{G})$ for metric graphs. It is routinely invoked, e.g., in the literature on ground states and standing waves for NLS on metric graphs (Adami–Serra–Tilli and many subsequent works), and in studies of NLS on specific tree-like graphs (tadpole, star, trees).

status_evidence.title: Non-Kirchhoff Vertices and Nonlinear Schrödinger Ground States on Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The most studied nonlinear PDE on a metric graph is the NLS with power nonlinearity; the Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in the energy space.
status_evidence.claim: NLS Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in the energy space on metric graphs.

status_evidence.title: Ground States for the Defocusing NLS on Non-Compact Metric Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The Cauchy problem for the defocusing NLS is globally well-posed on the energy space and conserves mass and energy.
status_evidence.claim: Global well-posedness in the energy space with conservation of mass and energy on noncompact metric graphs (which include trees).
